executed.claim: Default CSV parsing and default JSON encoding silently mishandle malformed/heterogeneous records, so an explicit data contract (field-count check, quarantine, canonical value encoding) is required rather than naive coercion.
executed.input: 4-row synthetic CSV 'a,b' with a short row, a long row, an empty-first-field row with Unicode value 'café, NA'; nan-valued dict
executed.expected_behavior: DictReader fills missing field with None (restval), parks extra field under None (restkey); naive numeric coercion raises ValueError on 'café, NA'; json.dumps emits non-standard NaN token; strict parse of that token fails; explicit contract check reports [(1,'short_row'), (2,'extra_fields')]. Expectations justified by documented stdlib csv/json defaults, verified in-sandbox.
executed.stdout:
dict_rows: [{"a": "1", "b": "2"}, {"a": "3", "b": null}, {"a": "4", "b": "5", "null": ["6"]}, {"a": "", "b": "café, NA"}]
coercion_errors: [(3, "could not convert string to float: 'café, NA'")]
json_payload: {"v": NaN, "u": "caf\u00e9", "ts": "2026-10-06T00:00:00Z"}
strict_json_accepted: False
contract_errors: [(1, 'short_row'), (2, 'extra_fields')]
W1_OK

executed.claim: The output status model works as specified: displayed cell order differs from execution order; an upstream edit invalidates ALL transitive downstream outputs (stale); a kernel restart makes prior-session outputs unverified (never current); a failed run is labeled failed without touching downstream.
executed.input: 3-cell chain c0→c1→c2 (hash-addressed sources), session S1 executed in order c2,c0,c1; then c0 edited; then restart to S2; then failed c0 run in S2
executed.expected_behavior: S1 all current; after edit {c0,c1,c2} all stale via transitive invalidation through recorded output fingerprints; after restart all unverified; after failed c0 run {c0: failed, c1: unverified, c2: unverified}
executed.stdout:
display order:        ['c0', 'c1', 'c2']
S1 execution order:   [('c2', 1, 'S1'), ('c0', 2, 'S1'), ('c1', 3, 'S1')]  (differs from display order c0,c1,c2)
S1 statuses:          {'c0': 'current', 'c1': 'current', 'c2': 'current'}
after editing c0:     {'c0': 'stale', 'c1': 'stale', 'c2': 'stale'}  (transitive invalidation)
after kernel restart: {'c0': 'unverified', 'c1': 'unverified', 'c2': 'unverified'}  (restart never marks old outputs current)
after failed run c0:  {'c0': 'failed', 'c1': 'unverified', 'c2': 'unverified'}
W2_OK

executed.claim: A bounded chunked streaming path aggregates a CSV with memory proportional to the chunk, not the file, with exact results.
executed.input: 100,000-row synthetic CSV ('i,square') built in memory (~1.64 MB), chunk bound 10,000 rows
executed.expected_behavior: count=100000, sum=4999950000, sq_sum=333328333350000 (verified against closed-form totals); max rows held ≤ chunk bound
executed.stdout:
rows=100000 sum=4999950000 sq_sum=333328333350000
source_bytes=1642650 max_rows_held=10000 (chunk bound 10000)
approx per-chunk buffer bytes=85176 => bounded memory per chunk, not O(file)
W3_OK

proposed_unexecuted.claim: Two-machine reopen of an exported bundle re-verifies dataset hashes, rebuilds env from lockfile, marks outputs unverified until re-run.
Replay equivalence: same notebook + pinned env + fresh kernel twice yields identical tabular output digests for deterministic cells.
Crash recovery: SIGKILL during save leaves journal-repairable state; affected outputs reopen as unverified, never current.
